_comment: R18 — found by running the consulting-week matrix against a live org, which is exactly where an external audit predicted it: 'Apex tests are the sharp case, they mutate org state while feeling read-only to a practitioner.' `sf apex run test` was classified as anonymous Apex because the match was on sub[:2] and both spellings begin (apex, run). The LEGACY form force:apex:test:run had been excluded since TQ-011; the modern form never was — the same two-spellings-one-handled shape LEGACY_TO_MODERN exists for. The cost was an UNSATISFIABLE refusal: the apex class demands the operator-approved copy at ~/.torque/approved/<digest>.apex, and `apex run test` takes no --file, so there was no digest to approve and no way for an operator to clear it. Running the suite before a deploy is ordinary work. The deny fixtures sit alongside deliberately: the fix must not buy the allows by making anonymous Apex reachable.

fixtures.id: R18 allow: apex run test is a test, not anonymous Apex
R18 allow: apex run test with a class filter

tool_input.command: sf apex run test --class-names MyTest --target-org sf-coffee
